newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end up in nervous, pre-budget trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end up in nervous, pre-budget trade.

text.p: Delhi shares ended higher in nervous pre-budget trade on Friday on select bids by foreign funds and speculators, traders said.
The Delhi bourse's benchmark index finished 2.00 points higher at 746.41.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is scheduled to present the annual budget for 1997/98 (April-March) to parliament at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT).
Traders said funds and speculators were bidders on hopes that Chidambaram would announce some favourable proposals for capital markets.

"Stock prices firmed up on sizeable purchases by foreign funds and speculators in the pre-budget session on expectations of some sops to industry and capital markets," said B.K. Nagpal, at brokers B.B. Portfolio.
Cement maker ACC rose 54 rupees to 1,493.
Shares of ITC spurted 10.40 rupees to end at 406.60.
A special post-budget trading session is scheduled from 6 to 8 p.m. (1230-1430 GMT)
